name: sgs/social-icons
title: SGS Social Icons
description: Row of social media platform icons with links. Supports Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X, YouTube, TikTok, WhatsApp, and more, plus a custom-SVG platform for anything else. Configurable size, style, theme-vs-brand colour, and hover colour; each icon's link (open-in-new-tab, rel) is set per-item via the shared SgsLinkControl; a Site-Info source mode renders the SAME list edited once in Appearance > SGS Site Info everywhere the block is placed (header/footer/drawer). Each icon item shape: { platform: string, url: string, label?: string, customIconUrl?: string, customIconId?: number, opensInNewTab?: boolean, rel?: string }. The accessible name (aria-label, WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2) is auto-generated per platform (e.g. "Follow us on Instagram") and always operator-editable via the label field.

sgs._imageControlsNote: Deliberate opt-out (FR-36-21). The universal image-controls extension (object-position/max-width/height) targets ONE block-level image; this block's optional custom-SVG upload is a PER-ITEM glyph inside a repeater (mirrors sgs/icon's own imageControls:false). Size is governed by the existing iconSize control instead.

wrapper.label: Wrapper
wrapper._note: Root <div> (render.php get_block_wrapper_attributes, style.css .sgs-social-icons — display:flex is hardcoded CSS, no attribute, so no `layer` is declared and the 12 arrangement members are honestly never asked about). No `layout` box-model attrs beyond padding/margin/gap exist (no width/height/max-width/border/box-shadow control) — honest gaps. Typography migrated off native WP support onto the shared TypographyControls/sgs_typography_css_rule() mechanism (D971/D972), root prefix '' (fontSize/fontWeight/fontStyle/lineHeight). The old native `textAlign` capability (`css:text-align`) was dropped, not replaced: this root is `display:flex` (style.css) with no inline/block content of its own, so `text-align` was inert dead CSS on every real instance — confirmed by reading style.css, not assumed.

icon.label: Icon
icon._note: Per-item <span class="sgs-social-icons__icon" aria-hidden="true"> — the decorative glyph itself (svg/img), render.php:451. Carries no colour attrMap: the `item` element's background/border/glyph attrs (below) do NOT paint this span, they paint the surrounding link box.

item.label: Icon Link
item._note: The clickable <a class="sgs-social-icons__item"> link box (render.php:462) — declared 2026-08-15 (Class 3, session fix: this element previously existed only in real markup, never in the manifest, an undeclared-sub-element drift the reseed audit flagged as an orphan `css_element`). D643: `iconColour`/`iconColourHover` were split (2026-08-16) into one attribute PER real CSS property. Pre-split, the resting/hover colour var (`--sgs-social-colour`/`--sgs-social-hover`) was consumed by up to THREE different declarations depending on `iconStyle` (plain: color only, style.css:20/34; filled: background, :45/52; outlined: border-color AND color SIMULTANEOUSLY — the base rule's `color` isn't overridden by the outlined selector, so both apply at once, :20+:57-65) — a single gradient-capable value cannot serve background/border/currentColor at once, so each property now has its own attribute (`iconBackground`/`iconBorderColour`/`iconGlyphColour`, each with a matching `*Hover` pair), each defaulting to the ORIGINAL shared default (text-muted resting / primary hover). clusters widened to text+fill+layout 2026-08-16 (D643): the D643 split gave this element attrMap entries for css:background-color and css:border-color, but with clusters=['text'] neither is a resolvable member, so the entries never reached claimedAttrs and iconBackground/iconBorderColour surfaced as STYLE-DEFECT orphans. background-color lives in the fill cluster and border-color in the layout cluster - declaring both is what makes the existing attrMap entries actually bind. Verified by running the gate, not by reasoning.

iconDecorative._comment: Spec 35 item 18 / {element}Decorative convention, scoped to the repeater item. Default true documents render.php's existing, always-correct WCAG pattern: the glyph /

iconGlyphColourGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting every icon's stroke instead of a flat colour. Non-empty wins over iconGlyphColour at render time (D636/D644).

iconGlyphColourHoverGradient.description: Hover-state sibling of iconGlyphColourGradient. Non-empty wins over iconGlyphColourHover on :hover.
